notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My one attempt to load the sources failed with an error saying I had no tool calls left, so I never read any of the pages. That included Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and the NET Bible notes.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Without any pages, anything I wrote would come from my own memory, which is exactly what you asked me to avoid. So I've left out all three parts: the traditional reading, where Protestant traditions differ, and the other views.

If you run the request again in a new turn, I'll begin by reading these verse-by-verse pages:
- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/proverbs-21/
- https://www.preceptaustin.org/proverbs-21-commentary
- https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/proverbs-21.html (Gill)
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/proverbs/21.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/proverbs/21.htm
- https://netbible.org/bible/Proverbs+21 (translator notes)

Next I'd search the tradition sites (Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Wesley Center, LCMS, New Advent and others) on the verses most likely to show real differences:
- **v. 1:** God's control of the king's heart (sovereignty and human choice).
- **v. 3 and v. 27:** Doing right versus offering sacrifice.
- **v. 14:** The secret gift or bribe.
- **v. 18:** The wicked as a "ransom" for the righteous.
- **v. 5, 17, 20 and 26:** Wealth and poverty, including any prosperity-teaching discussion.

Then I'd write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point, as you asked.
